text:
maria: Heads-up — had a bad triage yesterday. Node gauss-12 went into degraded, pods evicted, dmesg showed multiple Xid entries (79) but our logging only had the last 2k dmesg lines so we missed the full context. Slow to attribute to a flaky card.

ajay: Ugh. Do you have a snippet? we currently rotate dmesg aggressively (10k) to keep disk usage down.

maria: Paste of the important bits below (redacted node info):

```
[2026-03-15T02:12:03.123456] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00.0): 79, pid=2142, graphics fault
[2026-03-15T02:12:03.123467] nvidia-modeset: GPU 0000:65:00.0: Prime for display
[2026-03-15T02:12:03.123480] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2142 (python) score 1000 or sacrifice child
[2026-03-15T02:12:03.123495] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00.0): 31, pid=0, general fault
[2026-03-15T02:12:03.123510] kworker/3:2: GPU-cc3: framework timeout
```

journalctl -u pods-something.service --since "5 minutes ago" also showed the container OOM around the same time. We only had partial dmesg before because of rotation.

sasha: That Xid 79 + OOM pattern is a classic memory corruption/driver state problem, often flaky card or bad driver interop. We need a deterministic bundle collected at error time: full dmesg (with timestamps), journalctl -k, `nvidia-smi -q -x` (XML) or `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.total,memory.used,temperature.gpu --format=csv,noheader,nounits`, and the PCI bus id -> container mapping.

ajay: Agreed. Proposal: implement a transient collector that triggers on any NVRM Xid or on NIC/GPU ECC parity events. Collector should: 
- run `dmesg --ctime --kernel --human --show-dropped --level=err,warn,crit` with `--since` 10m and full ring snapshot if available
- run `journalctl -k --since "15 minutes ago"`
- run `nvidia-smi -q -x` and `nvidia-smi topo -m`
- capture `ls -l /dev/dri /dev/nvidia*` and `udevadm info --query=all --name=/dev/nvidia0`
- call the node metadata service to get instance-id/region and the kubelet to map PCI -> pod (via device plugin annotations)
- upload bundle to secure S3 and attach link to the alert

maria: That looks good. We should gate collection by a cheap heuristic so we don't run it on transient noise (eg only if Xid appears >1 in 30s or Xid code in [31,79,43] OR ECC corrected error count delta > 10).

sasha: Parsing rules for quick attribution in logs DB:
- regex: `Xid \(PCI:?(?P<pci>[^\)]+)\): (?P<code>\d+)` to extract PCI bus and code
- map code -> severity (e.g., 31/79 -> high, 43 -> medium)
- correlate PCI -> gpu_index via `/sys/bus/pci/devices/$PCI/vendor` and `/proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/*/information`

ajay: We should also enhance fluent-bit input to tag any journal/dmesg documents that contain `NVRM` or `Xid` so they appear in the error stream index. For full dumps keep them out of hot ES index to save cost — store as S3 + small indexed metadata doc (timestamp, pci, code, node, instance-id, bundle_url).

maria: Nice. How do we reconcile bus IDs with container-level device files so SREs can know which pod used the card?

sasha: On nodes with kube device plugin we annotate pods with `nvidia.com/gpu-pci` or `node-surgeon` writes `pciToPod` in `/var/lib/node-surgeon/gpu_mapping.json`. If that isn't available fallback to matching container cgroup device lists against major/minor of `/dev/nvidia0` and correlate with `lxcfs`/kubelet inspection. We'll include a script in the collector that tries these heuristics.

ajay: Implementation notes: collector as a systemd oneshot triggered by kernel netlink event (NVRM) or by node-exporter alert rule. Keep it low-priv (needs CAP_SYSLOG to read dmesg? we can use `journalctl -k`) and an RBAC pod agent that has permission to query kubelet.

maria: Retention + cost: index only metadata for 90 days, keep full bundles for 7 days in hot S3 tier then move to cold for 60 days. If bundle download requested escalate retention.

sasha: Also add a small parser that extracts common stack traces and attachment of `Xid` -> last user-space PIDs seen (from `ps` snapshot) so oncall can quickly decide drain vs replace.

ajay: I'll prototype the collector script now. rough sketch: 
```
#!/bin/sh
PCI="$1" # e.g. 0000:65:00.0
OUT=/tmp/gpu-bundle-$PCI-$(date +%s)
mkdir -p "$OUT"
dmesg --ctime --kernel --level=err,warn,crit --since "15 minutes ago" > "$OUT/dmesg.txt"
journalctl -k --since "20 minutes ago" > "$OUT/journal-kernel.txt"
nvidia-smi -q -x > "$OUT/nvidia-smi.xml" || echo "nvidia-smi failed" > "$OUT/nvidia-smi.err"
ps aux > "$OUT/ps.txt"
# add mapping heuristics
# tar + upload
```

maria: Nice. keep the bundle under 10MB if possible (strip huge /proc maps) and sign uploads.

infra-bot: Created alert INCIDENT-2026-87 and uploaded bundle to https://s3.redwood-internal/gpu-bundles/1801234567-65-00-0.tar.gz :thumbsup: 

sasha: :thumbsup: Next steps: ajay prototype + a short RFC for the collector and parsing rules. I'll sketch the parsing rules to run in ES ingest pipeline and share.

maria: Thanks — if prototype looks good we flip on for prod pilot in us-west-2 on a subset of nodes (20). Keep me in the loop.

ajay: Will do. starting now. :coffee:
